headline: High-risk filesystem and network overlap: Replit Agent can write broad Repl state while unstructured can read/write files and egress, creating default-path leakage and action-conflict risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can read and write Repl workspace files and B can read/write documents, so file-based prompt injection is plausible if either agent consumes the other's outputs as trusted content. No shared clipboard/MCP is shown, so the pathway is not maximal, but shared files are enough to create default-risk injection.
conditions: IF agent_a writes instructions into a workspace file that agent_b later parses as content, injection is possible.
IF agent_b emits document text that agent_a treats as trusted guidance, injection is possible.
mitigations: Separate input and output directories for the two agents.
Add a manual review step before either agent consumes the other's files.
Prefix exchanged files with a strict schema and reject free-form instructions.
Use read-only mounts for one agent's inputs where possible.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and content-type enforcement.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches secrets and deployment configuration and has broad network egress; B touches documents and text and can egress to allowlisted endpoints. If sensitive Repl files are placed in shared documents or passed through B, leakage can occur in default workflows. The profiles do not show a shared workspace, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF secrets or deployment configs from agent_a are copied into files processed by agent_b, leakage is possible.
IF agent_b sends extracted document contents to allowlisted external services, sensitive data can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of any files handed to unstructured.
Disable external uploads for sensitive documents.
Use separate workspaces or containers for each agent.
Redact secrets before document processing.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP scanning on handoff files.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files and spawn subprocesses, and A can also modify git state while B can write files in its own container. If they are pointed at the same mutable workspace, concurrent edits and git corruption are plausible and can cause irreversible loss. The profiles do not prove shared locking, so uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to operate on the same repository directory, write conflicts can occur.
IF agent_a commits or rebases while agent_b edits the same files, git state corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Serialize write access with a lock file.
Disable git writes for one agent during the other's run.
Snapshot the workspace before concurrent runs.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can generate code or configuration that B may ingest as document text, and B can transform that content without an explicit verification step shown in the profiles. This creates a plausible cascade where A's mistakes are amplified by B's downstream processing, but no direct autonomous action like email or deployment is documented.
conditions: IF agent_b treats agent_a's generated files as authoritative source material, errors can propagate.
IF agent_a writes malformed configs that agent_b extracts or reformats, the mistake can be amplified.
mitigations: Require a human review before B processes A's outputs.
Add validation checks on A-generated files.
Compare B outputs against source documents.
Limit B to read-only transformation of vetted inputs.
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: A handles secrets and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl environment, while B processes documents and images with allowlisted network egress. If regulated or sensitive documents are routed from A into B, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not specify HIPAA/GDPR status, so this is a compliance-risk estimate rather than a confirmed violation.
conditions: IF EU personal data or regulated documents are processed by both agents under different retention policies, compliance mismatch occurs.
IF secrets from agent_a are embedded into documents sent to agent_b, policy scope may expand unexpectedly.
mitigations: Classify data before handoff.
Keep regulated data out of B unless policy is confirmed.
Document retention and deletion rules for both agents.
Use separate tenants or regions where required.
requires-engineering: map data flows to compliance controls.
